text.p: Fil-Estate Land Inc said on Monday its unaudited net income for the current fiscal year ended September soared by 130 percent to 1.805 billion pesos from the year-ago 783.5 million.
The real estate firm also said in a statement to the Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission that it expected its net income for fiscal year 1996/97 to reach 2.44 billion pesos.
The company attributed the rise in 1995/96 profits to robust demand for its real estate projects.
This pushed up the revenues of the firm to 6.883 billion pesos, up 118 percent from the previous year, Fil-Estate said.

"Of total revenues, 54 percent came from subdivision lot sales, 35 percent from sales of golf and resort shares, five percent from residential condominium unit sales, and six percent from other income sources," it added.

Fil-Estate also said 64 percent from its projected net income for fiscal year 1996/1997 will come from subdivision lot sales, 30 percent from golf and resort shares, and six percent from residential and office condominium sales.

Fifty-five percent of Fil-Estate's revenues will come from projects from the high-growth CALABARZON area, which stands for the towns of Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal and Quezon transformed into industrial estates by the government.
Projects in Metro Manila will account for 12 percent of the revenues, and the remaining from other growth areas in the country, Fil-Estate said.
